title: Dubrovnik vs Split: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Split for value, authenticity, and island-hopping access. Dubrovnik for pure visual spectacle and the bucket-list moment. Do both with 7 days in Croatia.

categories.name: Daily Budget
categories.summary: Split runs €60-90/day mid-range; Dubrovnik costs €100-140/day. Split is 30-40% cheaper across all categories.

categories.name: Visual Spectacle
categories.summary: Dubrovnik’s city walls and terracotta-roofed Old Town are among the most photogenic places in Europe.

categories.name: Old Town Authenticity
categories.summary: People actually live inside Diocletian’s Palace in Split. Dubrovnik’s Old Town is heavily touristic.

categories.name: Island Hopping
categories.summary: Split has direct ferries to Hvar, Brač, Vis, and Korčula. Dubrovnik island access is limited to Lokrum and Elafiti.

categories.name: Food Value
categories.summary: Split’s konobas in Varoš offer authentic Dalmatian food at fair prices. Dubrovnik inside the walls is expensive and tourist-oriented.

categories.name: Day Trips
categories.summary: Split accesses Trogir, Krka, Hvar, and Makarska. Dubrovnik reaches Mostar and Kotor (excellent but fewer options).

categories.name: Crowds (Jul-Aug)
categories.summary: Dubrovnik is severely overtouristed in peak summer with cruise ships. Split handles crowds better due to its larger size.

categories.name: Beaches
categories.summary: Split’s ferry access to island beaches (Zlatni Rat on Brač, Hvar coves) is far superior to Dubrovnik’s rocky city beaches.

categories.name: Getting There
categories.summary: Split Airport has more budget airline connections; Dubrovnik is more expensive to fly into.

categories.name: Nightlife
categories.summary: Split’s Bačvice beach bar scene and local clubs are more authentic than Dubrovnik’s tourist-oriented bar strip.

faq.question: Is Dubrovnik or Split better for first-time visitors to Croatia?
faq.answer: Split edges Dubrovnik for first-timers: Diocletian’s Palace, island-hopping access, and better value. Dubrovnik is bucket-list material but works best as 2-3 nights, then move to Split.

faq.question: How far is Dubrovnik from Split?
faq.answer: ~230km, 3-4 hours by bus (€15-25) or 2.5-3 hours by catamaran ferry in summer (€35-50).

faq.question: Is Dubrovnik worth visiting despite the overtourism?
faq.answer: Yes — the Old Town and city walls are genuinely spectacular. Visit in shoulder season (May, Sep-Oct) or early morning in peak summer.
